chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ammar ibn Marwan from al-Munakhkhal ibn Jamil from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you turn away from a prescribed prayer, do not turn away except with the departure of the curse of the Banu Umayya."

key_terms.لَعْنِ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ: The curse of the Banu Umayya

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'curse of Banu Umayya' in Shia prayer rulings?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual integrity of the five daily prayers to the concept of *al-ghurba* (alienation) and the enduring curse upon the Umayyad dynasty, which symbolizes deviation from divine truth. By keeping the 'curse of Banu Umayya' in mind, the believer anchors their devotion in the historical struggle between right and wrong, ensuring that ritual performance is accompanied by conscious fidelity to the Ahl al-Bayt. This practice transforms the prayer into an act of both worship and political-spiritual allegiance, reinforcing the believer's identity amidst a world of corruption.
